title: [Refurb] Apple MacBook Pro 14" M1 Pro 16GB RAM 512GB SSD $828 Delivered / QLD C&C @ Australian Computer Traders
body:
Deal: [Refurb] Apple MacBook Pro 14" M1 Pro 16GB RAM 512GB SSD $828 Delivered / QLD C&C @ Australian Computer Traders

[mskeggs] The linked m1 has 16gb and 512gb. Which I guess makes it more acceptable in this day and age.
Is it a good deal for someone not going to be cpu blocked? I think yes if you are using it for office apps etc, and want the benefits of a pro over an air. But m1 airs with 8gb are half the price and are fine for office computing too.
My rule of thumb is m1 will be fine for most cpu tasks for years yet, so the ram and storage are going to be the constraints.
FWIW, I will take the gamble ram and storage bubble will pop before my hand-me-down m1 air becomes an issue.
[Ipodisclassic] This seems like a great deal given that computer hardware is getting more expensive due to AI. I’d buy this if I hadn’t bought an M5 air before the price hikes in July.
[joshx] my 2c…
16gb is fine (in this economy, not in general..) for most people, IMHO.
Especially on the newer Mac hardware where it's a lot better (IMHO) than Windows. I won't mention Linux, as I said for most people they just want something basic.
The "Apple Silicon" (M series) are honestly great hardware, it's just the absolute shitshow of software. Being able to close the lid, resume properly, without draining battery etc, is great.
A key issue some people miss is that cheaper/lowend Macbooks (the Neos, for example) with less memory use a lot of swap (where it writes the memory to disk), and it kills the disk.
Given the neos etc have lowish TB endurance (from what I recall), there are reports of rapidly killed disks.
The battery is another issue, Apple just seemed to replace mine when I had another issue on my MacBook Pro (14-inch, 2023) m2 when I had another warranty issue.
I just checked my Macbook Air m1, which I've had since around ~2021-06-28, and I stopped using it for a while, has Data Units Written: 85,599,424 [43.8 TB] according to smartctl -a disk0 . So this is 2% for the m1/3% for the m2 (~2023-07-08). (Implied lifetime 1,750-2,900 TB for m1 air, 2,400-3,400 TB for m2 pro, from my quick math.)
My newer m2 (yes, I bought the (profanity) m2 that had 2 releases in a year, FML), has Data Units Written: 164,388,772 [84.1 TB] , but I also do a lot of disk operations (code compiling, etc). That's way less than I thought. I still have AppleCare+ for this device (I let the other one lapse, FML), so hopefully
[Merlict] I feel like the disk wear thing is blown way of proportion.
M1 / M2 airs have been running on 8gb writing to the SSD for many years and the vast majority are fine.
[joshx] Agreed. I was curious (my long rambly post), so I shared personal stats, I haven't seen the actual Neo numbers, and honestly there is so much FUD/clickbait (because (profanity) apple, amirite).
For most peoples actual day-to-use, it'll be the battery.
Not sure how much that costs to replace aftermarket, or the experience to do this yourself or just have a repair place do it for you (seems to be ~$200AUD?).
But might be worth checking with Apple as well, to see if you can get a replacement outside of warranty.
[Merlict] @joshx: Official apple battery replacement for this MBP is $439, ouch
[arvindat] A Pro-tier 14" M1 MacBook for $828 AUD shipped is insane value. Though a used one but defintely a powerhouse, keep an eye on the usage and condition.12-month warranty is a Plus.
[ssfps] insane value
It's decent value, hardly insane. I have one of these, and it's great, but it's out of warranty (5 years old) and spare parts/repairs are going to be expensive and more unavailable as it ages. It's not like an old thinkpad where a 5 year old device can be kept going for peanuts until 10,15 years old.
[xavierod] Legend for posting. Only got the b tier but been waiting for a deal like this. Beat up ones are a $1k elsewhere
[billbob123454] For those who missed out, eBay can have some refurbished gems if you can match it with the right coupon. I got this laptop but the 32gb version for $949 a couple weeks ago. Needed a clean and that was about it.
[User0001] I bought this last time when it was a bit cheaper. Great computer in 2026. Can edit 4k video on it, display is gorgeous and looks identical to the newest ones (purchase better display to access all 1600 nits).
[Hamlet] Wow, I got the 16" M1 Pro for like $3k back in 2022… I'm not sure if I'm more surpirsed that it's so cheap now or whether time has just flown by quickly. Computer still performing well and hasn't missed a beat…
